findings.premise: The bounded wait and the handed measure address root causes 1 and 3 of the ISSUE at the place they occur: one wait in measureConnection covers both the single-source and the pool path, and the context builder gets a way to be handed the run's measure.
findings.evidence: src/analyze/measure.ts:444-494: measureConnection is the only function that awaits `pool.acquire(id)` (456) and the unbounded listings `r.listTables({ complete: true })` (466), `k.listNamespaces({ complete: true })` (476), `listFilesForConnection` (484). measureDataSource calls it at 438; measureDataPool calls it directly at 512 (`await measureConnection(pool, id, undefined)`), not through measureDataSource, as the design says. No signal or timer exists anywhere in the file today. src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1372-1378 reads only `{ intent, sizeHint }` from the input and always measures, so it has no way to be handed a measure, which is root cause 3. src/daemon/db/pool.ts:131-136 shares `entry.building` between callers, so abandoning the wait does not start a second connection attempt. findings.premise: The design leaves out nothing from the ISSUE's second fix intent: 'a file or a symbol scope does not cause every entity of its repository to be read'.
findings.evidence: The design narrows only the measure's own read (measureStoredArea, measure.ts:344). On the production path the same request still reads every entity of the repository: measureRequestScope resolves through resolveTaskScope (measure.ts:294), which for code and docs calls ensureNonEmptyClosure (task-scope.ts:73-74), which does `await listEntitiesForRepo(null, best.path)` and only reads `.length` (invariants.ts:234-237). The design states this one read openly and defers it to ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0, so its own accounting ('one whole-repository read where it causes two today') is correct per call of measureRequestScope. It is still a part of the fix intent that is not delivered. Two further whole-repository reads in the same run are not mentioned: the builder's own `ensureNonEmptyClosure(scope)` for a code run (context/driver.ts:379-380) and the run driver's `resolveTaskScope(intent.scopeRef, intent.target, 'the run')` before planning (orchestrator/driver.ts:368-370). A symbol scope also pays a full entity-table scan while it is resolved (`deps.findEntitiesByFile(filePath)`, context/scope.ts:205), before any measure is taken. findings.premise: The store offers a point read by id and a per-file read; the per-file read has no index and passes over every row of the entity table of all repositories, so a file scope saves only the building of the other files' entities.
findings.evidence: src/db/entities.ts:585-593 getEntity: `store.entityIdByString.get(id)` then `readEntityRow(store, u64)`, no range scan. 795-811 findEntitiesByFile: `for (const { key, value } of store.entity.getRange())`, decodes each row, resolves its repo path and compares `toAbsolutePath(row.filePath, repoPath) !== file`; it takes no repository argument, so rows of every repository are visited. The design's modest statement of the saving is right for a further reason it does not give: listEntitiesForRepo (779-793) also walks `store.entity.getRange()` over the whole table and decodes every row, skipping only on `row.repoId !== repoId`. So neither read avoids the table scan today; the narrow read saves the id lookup and entity construction for the repository's other files. [files: src/db/entities.ts]
findings.action: None. When building, keep the comment on the file read honest about this (both reads scan the table until ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0).

(1) Without the fix the ac1 and ac2 tests hang instead of failing an assertion; give each a short per-test timeout so the falsifying run fails fast and visibly. (2) The run-level ac5 test must count a reader that only the measure uses (`listEntities` of MeasureDeps), not the scope readers' `listEntitiesForRepo`, which the index checks call several times in a run (task-scope.ts:74, context/driver.ts:380, orchestrator/driver.ts:370) and would hide the difference.

summary.prose: Measuring a request no longer waits without limit on a live data source: each source is given 120 seconds by default (a setting) to be reached and listed, and one that does not answer is reported as a size that could not be determined, with the reason; a cancelled request stops measuring. For a request scoped to one symbol the measure reads that one entity; for a request scoped to one file it no longer builds every stored entity of the repository, though the store's entity table is still scanned for a file, because the store has no index by file (ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0 is filed for that index). The saving is in the measure's own read: resolving a code or docs scope still reads the repository once to check that it is indexed, and that read is left to the same issue. A run measures the area it names once: it hands that measure to the context builder, which uses it and takes none of its own, while a caller that hands none is measured by the builder as before.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Design the fix for ISSUE-008e146ad1475ef9: (1) the measure of a live data source is taken within a bounded time (default 120 seconds per source, by the stakeholder's decision of 2026-10-10, changeable by configuration), a source that does not answer in time is reported as not determined with a reason that says the listing timed out, and a cancelled request stops measuring; (2) the stored area read for a measure is no wider than the scope needs (a file or symbol scope does not read every entity of its repository) with unchanged counts; (3) one run takes one measure of the area it names: the context built for a run uses the run's measure and takes none of its own, while a caller that has taken none still gets one from the context builder.

api.name: measureRequestScope
api.signature: measureRequestScope(scopeRef: AnalyzeScopeRef, target: AnalyzeTarget, sizeHint?: AnalyzeScope, options?: MeasureOptions): Promise<RequestMeasure>

parameters.name: scopeRef
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: the scope the request names.

parameters.name: sizeHint
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: a stated size, kept as the hint.

parameters.name: options
parameters.purpose: New. `signal`: the request's cancellation signal. `sourceTimeoutMs`: the time one live data source is given, in place of the configured value. Passed on to measureResolvedScope.

returns.meaning: Unchanged in shape. Two new reasons for a measure that is not determined: a live source that did not answer within the limit, and a request that was cancelled. One read this design does not change: for a code or docs request the scope is resolved through resolveTaskScope, whose index check (ensureNonEmptyClosure in src/analyze/context/invariants.ts) asks the store for every entity of the repository to see that it holds any. So through measureRequestScope a file or symbol scope of a code or docs request causes one whole-repository read, the index check, where it causes two today (the index check and the measure's own read); through measureResolvedScope, with a scope already resolved, it causes none. Answering the index check without building the repository's entities is recorded on ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0. That issue also holds the other reads of the same kind that a run makes and that this design does not touch: the context builder's own index check for a code run (src/analyze/context/driver.ts), the run driver's scope check before planning (src/analyze/orchestrator/driver.ts), and the scan of the entity table made while a symbol scope is resolved (src/analyze/context/scope.ts). What this design delivers of the issue's second point is therefore the measure's own read, and no more.

postconditions: With no options the result is today's for every scope that answers within the configured limit.

api.name: measureResolvedScope
api.signature: measureResolvedScope(scope: ResolvedScope, target: AnalyzeTarget, sizeHint?: AnalyzeScope, options?: MeasureOptions): Promise<RequestMeasure>

returns.meaning: As today, with these changes. (1) When the signal is already aborted on entry, nothing is read and the measure is not determined with the note `the request was cancelled before it was measured`. (2) A data request on a repo, workspace or manifest directory measures its connections one after another as today; before each one the signal is checked, and once it has fired the remaining connections are not asked and the measure is not determined with the note `the request was cancelled while its data sources were being measured`. (3) A stored area is read as narrowly as its scope allows: for a symbol scope the one entity is read by its id; for a file scope the entities of that file are read; in both cases only entities of the scope's repository are counted, and when the narrow read finds none the area is read as today (every entity of the repository), so the result, including `the repository holds no stored entity`, is today's. Any other scope is read as today. What this saves for a file scope is limited, and is stated here as it is: the store has no index by file, so the read of one file's entities (findEntitiesByFile in src/db/entities.ts) still passes over every row of the entity table, of all repositories, and works out each row's path; it saves only the building of the entities of the repository's other files. Reading a file's rows without that scan needs an index by repository and file, which is ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0 and is not part of this design. The symbol read is a point read and scans nothing.

postconditions: For a symbol or file scope the counts (`items`, `files`) and the size equal those the whole-repository read gives.
A symbol scope whose entity is found in its repository causes no read of the repository's entities.

api.name: measureDataSource
api.signature: measureDataSource(scope: DataScope, sizeHint?: AnalyzeScope, options?: MeasureOptions): Promise<RequestMeasure>

parameters.name: scope
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: the pool path and the connection id.

returns.meaning: As today, except that reaching the source (the pool's acquire) and listing it (listTables, listNamespaces or the file listing, in complete mode) together are given one bounded wait of `sourceTimeoutMs`, or the configured limit when none is passed. When the wait ends first the measure is not determined with the note `the listing of '<id>' timed out: the source did not answer within <n> seconds`. When the signal fires first it is not determined with the note `the request was cancelled while the source '<id>' was being measured`. The limit is per source: a data request on a repository with several connections gives each its own. The wait is abandoned, not the driver's call: the drivers have no cancellation, so the call may go on in the background; its later result is dropped and its later rejection is caught and logged at debug level. Where the wait lives: in measureConnection, the private function of src/analyze/measure.ts that reaches one connection (`pool.acquire(id)`) and lists it, and that both measureDataSource and measureDataPool call. measureDataPool, which measures the connections registered at a repo, workspace or manifest directory one after another and calls measureConnection directly (it does not go through measureDataSource), is changed with it: it takes the options, checks the signal before each connection and passes the options to each call of measureConnection. Loading the pool (`acquireDataPool` and `pool.reload()`, in measureDataSource and in measureDataPool) is not inside the wait: it reads the connections file and closes the drivers of connections that were removed from it, and is not bounded by this design.

postconditions: A source that timed out or was cancelled is never returned as a count: `determined` is false, `items` and `files` are 0 and the size is XL.
The checks made before the source is reached (no connection named, a kind whose listing is a sample of keys) are unchanged and are not subject to the wait.

dataModelChanges.details: export interface MeasureOptions { readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; readonly sourceTimeoutMs?: number | undefined }. `sourceTimeoutMs` is the time one live data source is given to be reached and listed; left out, the configured value is used. A value that is not a finite number greater than 0 is treated as left out.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + export interface MeasureOptions { readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; readonly sourceTimeoutMs?: number | undefined }

dataModelChanges.details: A new entry of the configuration catalog (src/config/config-catalog.ts), in the group 'Analysis & memory': type number, default 120000, described as the time in milliseconds one live data source is given to answer when a request is measured. It is read from ~/.insrc/config.json each time a live source is measured (not cached), by a reader that never throws and returns 120000 when the file is absent or unparseable or the value is missing or is not a finite number greater than 0, in the manner of the reader of `codeReview.freshnessTimeoutMs`. Being in the catalog, the setting is kept by the daemon's configuration reconcile and shown by the settings screens that list the catalog.

RunShapeInput (src/analyze/context/types.ts) gains `readonly measure?: RequestMeasure | undefined`: the measure the caller has already taken of the area this intent's scope names. When it is given and its source is 'named-area' or 'data-source', the exploration pipeline (src/analyze/context/driver.ts) uses it for its planning call and does not measure; when it is absent, or its source is 'lookup-results' (which is not a measure of a named area), the pipeline measures as today. The field is left out of the bundle cache key (keyedInputs), as the intent's size and the stated size already are, so a run's bundle is cached under the same key whether or not a measure was handed in. The caller is trusted to hand a measure of the same scope reference and target as the intent; the run driver takes both from the same intent.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: ~ RunShapeInput { intent; sizeHint?; + measure?: RequestMeasure | undefined }

dataModelChanges.details: PlanBuilderOpts (src/analyze/planner/types.ts) gains `readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined`. The recursive planner passes it to the measure of each child plan and uses it for nothing else. The run driver sets it from its own signal.

MeasureDeps gains two optional readers beside `listEntities`: `getEntity?: (id: string) => Promise<Entity | null>` and `listEntitiesOfFile?: (file: string) => Promise<readonly Entity[]>`. In production they are getEntity and findEntitiesByFile of src/db/entities.ts. A test stands in counting readers to show which read a scope causes.

dataModelChanges.entity: The run driver's and the plan RPC's use of the measure
dataModelChanges.details: runAnalyze (src/analyze/orchestrator/driver.ts) passes `{ signal }` to its one call of measureRequestScope and hands the measure it took to the context builder: buildRunBundle({ intent, measure }, ...). Today the builder measures the same resolved scope a second time; after the change one run takes one measure of the area it names, and the size on the run's intent and the size of the builder's planning call are the same value by construction. The plan RPC (the handler in src/daemon/analyze-rpc.ts that measures the request's intent and then calls buildRunBundle({ intent }, ...) before it runs the planner) has the same double measure and is changed the same way: it hands the measure it took to the builder. It has no cancellation signal and passes none. The callers that are unchanged: the classify RPC, the freeform probe and the analyze-step tool (which measures with its own call of measureResolvedScope in src/mcp/analyze-step/phases/start.ts and never calls the builder) each take one measure, pass no options and build no run context; the bundle RPC (which passes its caller's input to buildRunBundle as it is, and is what the one-shot analyze tool uses) hands no measure, and the builder measures for it as today. These three are the only production callers of buildRunBundle: the run driver, the plan RPC and the bundle RPC.

errorCases.scenario: A live data source does not answer: reaching it or listing it never finishes.
errorCases.detection: The bounded wait around the pool's acquire and the driver's listing ends before they do: a timer started when the source is first asked fires after the limit.
errorCases.response: The source's measure is not determined, with the note `the listing of '<id>' timed out: the source did not answer within <n> seconds`. The driver's call is left to finish or fail in the background; its result is dropped and its rejection is caught and logged at debug level. The request goes on.
errorCases.userImpact: The request is sized as the largest, the report's measure line says the size could not be determined and why, and the scope checks and the plan run as they do for any size that is not determined. Today the request waits in its classify stage for as long as the source takes.

errorCases.scenario: The request is cancelled while a live source is being measured.
errorCases.detection: The cancellation signal passed in the options fires: the bounded wait listens for its abort event, and the signal's state is checked before each source of a pool and on entry to the pass.
errorCases.response: The wait ends at once, no further source is asked, and the measure is not determined with a note that says the request was cancelled. The run driver's own check for cancellation, made right after the measure, then ends the run as cancelled, as it does today between stages.
errorCases.userImpact: A cancelled request stops within the measure and does not wait for the source.

errorCases.scenario: A data request on a repository names several connections and one of them does not answer.
errorCases.detection: As the first case, for that connection; each connection has its own wait.
errorCases.response: The other connections are measured as today. The sum is not a count: the measure is not determined and its note lists the connection that timed out with its reason and the number of objects counted in the others, in today's form for a connection that could not be counted.
errorCases.userImpact: The wait is at most the limit for each connection that does not answer, one after another: with the default, two stalled connections cost four minutes.

errorCases.scenario: The abandoned call of a driver that timed out later fails, or later succeeds.
errorCases.detection: The call's promise settles after the wait has ended.
errorCases.response: A rejection is caught where the wait was set up, so it is never an unhandled rejection of the daemon, and is logged at debug level with the connection id. A late result is dropped. The measure already returned is not changed.
errorCases.userImpact: None. The connection the pool holds for that source may stay busy until the driver's own call ends; a later task that uses the same connection may wait on it, as it would today.

errorCases.scenario: The setting holds a value that cannot be a time limit (not a number, not finite, zero or negative), or the configuration file cannot be read.
errorCases.detection: The setting's reader checks the type and the range of the value and catches a failed read or parse.
errorCases.response: The default of 120000 ms is used. Nothing is thrown.
errorCases.userImpact: A mistyped setting does not stop requests from being measured.

errorCases.scenario: The narrow read of a symbol or a file scope fails (the store cannot be read).
errorCases.detection: The read rejects inside measureResolvedScope's existing try block.
errorCases.response: As today for a failed read: the measure is not determined with the note `the count could not be taken (<reason>)`.

edgeCases.input: A live source that answers within the limit.
edgeCases.expected: Today's measure, unchanged: the count of its tables, namespaces or files, or today's reason when the listing was cut, is not supported or failed.

edgeCases.input: A source whose kind lists a sample of keys (redis, valkey, keydb, etcd), or a scope that names no connection.
edgeCases.expected: Today's reason, returned before the source is reached; no wait is started.

edgeCases.input: A symbol scope whose entity is stored in the scope's repository.
edgeCases.expected: One point read; items 1, files 1 (0 when the entity has no file path), the size the whole-repository read gives; no read of the repository's entities by the measure. (The index check made while a code or docs scope is resolved still reads them once.)

edgeCases.input: A symbol scope whose entity is not found by its id, or is found in another repository.
edgeCases.expected: The area is read as today (every entity of the repository) and today's result is returned.

edgeCases.input: A file scope whose file has stored entities.
edgeCases.expected: The entities of that file are read, those of the scope's repository are counted, files is 1; the counts equal those of the whole-repository read. The read still passes over the rows of the entity table (ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0).

edgeCases.input: A file scope whose file has no stored entity (an indexed repository, a file with nothing in it), or a scope with no file path.
edgeCases.expected: The area is read as today: a count of 0 when the repository holds entities, not determined when it holds none.

edgeCases.input: A repo, workspace, module or directory scope.
The run driver hands the context builder a measure that is not determined (for example a source that timed out).
edgeCases.expected: The builder uses it as it is: the planning call is given the largest size, the same size the run's intent has. It does not measure again, so the source is not waited on a second time.

edgeCases.input: A caller hands the context builder a measure whose source is 'lookup-results'.
edgeCases.expected: It is not a measure of a named area: the builder ignores it and measures as today.

edgeCases.input: A caller of the context builder that hands no measure (the bundle RPC, which the one-shot analyze tool uses).
edgeCases.expected: The builder measures the resolved scope as today.

edgeCases.input: A child plan of a plan tree names a live source the root also named.
edgeCases.expected: The source is listed again for the child, within its own limit and under the run's signal. Listing a source once per run is not part of this design.

edgeCases.input: A signal that is already aborted when the pass is entered.
edgeCases.expected: Nothing is read; the measure is not determined with the note `the request was cancelled before it was measured`.
It is used in place of the configured value for that call; a value that is not a finite number greater than 0 is treated as not passed.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The measuring pass never throws: a count it cannot take is a measure that is not determined, with the largest size and the reason in its note.
A measure that is not determined has items 0 and files 0; a count taken of part of the area goes in the note, never in the counts.
The counts and the size of a named area are those of the entities the scope's area rule keeps (inAreaOf); the narrower reads return the same counts.
A count of zero is a count only when a registered repository contains the scope and holds stored entities; a repository with no stored entity is not determined.
The run's intent has its size before the context is built and before the scope checks: the `classified` event and the stored run record carry it.
The context builder is the writer of the size its planning call is given; a size on the intent it is handed is not read. A measure handed in beside the intent is the one exception this design adds.
The bundle cache key does not depend on the size or on a stated size; it does not depend on a handed measure either.
The store and the live sources are read one after another, never in parallel.

migration.stateBefore: The measuring pass takes no options: its waits on a live data source (the pool's acquire and the driver's complete listing) have no bound and no cancellation signal reaches it, although the run it is called from has one (s1: the reading of measure.ts and of the run driver). A stored area is measured by reading every entity of the repository and narrowing the list, for every kind of scope (s1: the reading of measure.ts and of the store's reads). The run driver measures the request and the context builder then measures the same resolved scope again for its planning call; the builder's input has no field for a measure already taken (s1: the reading of the callers). There is no setting for a time limit on a data source (s1: the search of the configuration catalog).
migration.stateAfter: The three exported measuring functions take an optional options argument with a cancellation signal and a time limit, and pass it to the two private functions that do the work on a live source: measureConnection, which holds the bounded wait, and measureDataPool, which checks the signal before each connection. Each live source is given one bounded wait, 120 seconds by default from the new setting `analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs`; a source that does not answer, and a request that is cancelled, give a measure that is not determined with its reason. A symbol scope is measured with a read by id and a file scope with the read of that file's entities (which still scans the entity table until ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0), with the whole-repository read as the fallback when the narrow read finds nothing. The run driver passes its signal to the measure and to the recursive planner, and hands its measure to the context builder, which uses it and does not measure; a caller that hands none is measured by the builder as before.

migrationSteps.action: Add the setting to the configuration catalog with its default and its reader; add the options argument to the three exported measuring functions and to the private measureConnection and measureDataPool; bound the wait on each live source in measureConnection and stop on the signal, checking it before each connection in measureDataPool. No caller passes options yet, so every caller gets the configured limit and no cancellation.
Read a symbol scope by id and a file scope by its file's entities, with the whole-repository read as the fallback; add the two readers to the pass's test seam.

Add the optional measure to the context builder's run input and leave it out of the bundle cache key; have the pipeline use a handed measure of a named area and measure otherwise. Add the optional signal to the planner's options. Have the run driver pass its signal to the measure and to the planner, and hand its measure to the context builder.
Update the guide (docs/daemon.md, where it describes how a request is measured and the settings) to state the time limit, its setting, the two new reasons, and that a run measures once.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API changes: the functions and types are internal to the analyze framework, and every addition is an optional argument or an optional field, so existing callers compile and behave as before. Behaviour that changes for a user: a data request on a source that takes longer than 120 seconds to be reached and listed used to wait and then be counted; it is now sized as the largest with the reason that the listing timed out, unless the setting is raised. No stored data is rewritten and no stored record changes shape: a measure that is not determined already exists and only gains two new reasons in its note. A configuration file written before the change has no value for the new setting and gets the default.

alternativesConsidered.name: Options on the measuring pass, and the run's measure handed to the context builder
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The measuring functions take an options argument (signal, time limit); the run passes its measure to the context builder in the builder's input.
alternativesConsidered.approach: measureRequestScope, measureResolvedScope and measureDataSource gain a last optional argument, MeasureOptions { signal?, sourceTimeoutMs? }. Each live source is given one bounded wait that covers reaching it and listing it; when the wait ends first the source is not determined with a reason that says the listing timed out, and when the signal fires the pass stops and returns not determined with a reason that says the request was cancelled. The default limit comes from a new setting in the configuration catalog (120 seconds). The stored-area read is chosen by the scope's kind: a point read for a symbol, the read of one file's entities for a file, today's read otherwise, with today's read as the fallback when the narrow read finds nothing. RunShapeInput gains an optional `measure`: the pipeline uses it for its planning call when given and measures as today when not. The run driver passes its measure and its signal; the recursive planner's options gain a signal for the child measures.
pros: Every caller keeps working unchanged: the new arguments and the new input field are optional.
One measure per run by construction: the size on the intent and the size of the planning call come from the same object.
The time limit and the cancellation live in one place, the pass, for every caller.
cons: Three signatures and one input type change.
The handed-down measure is trusted to be of the same scope; the type cannot check it.

alternativesConsidered.name: A measure cache keyed by run and scope
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The measuring pass remembers its result per run id, scope and target, so a second request for the same measure returns the first.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The pass keeps a map from (runId, scopeRef, target) to the measure taken. measureRequestScope and measureResolvedScope gain a runId argument and consult the map first. The context builder, which has the run id, gets the run driver's measure from the map without any change to its input; child plans that name the same source get the same listing. The time limit and the signal are added as in a1.
pros: The context builder's input does not change.
A source named by several child plans is listed once per run.
cons: Hidden shared state: when to drop an entry (end of run, failure, cancellation) must be got right or a later run under the same id reads a stale measure.
A measure that was not determined because of a time-out would be cached and never retried within the run; whether that is wanted is a decision of its own.
Two callers must pass the same key to agree; a mismatch silently measures twice again.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the double measure through shared state whose lifetime and keys must be got right; a stale or mismatched entry fails silently.

alternativesConsidered.name: The context builder is the only one that measures
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The run driver stops measuring; the context builder measures and returns the measure with its bundle, and the driver reads the size from there.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The run driver no longer calls measureRequestScope. buildRunBundle returns the measure it took (it already puts a measure on the bundle's report) and the driver sets the intent's size from it afterwards. The time limit and the signal are passed through the builder's options.
pros: One writer of the size in the run path.
cons: The run's `classified` event and the stored intent carry the size before the context is built today; they would have to wait for the multi-minute context build or be emitted without a size.
The scope checks and the abort check that run between classify and plan would act on an intent with no size.
The measure on the bundle's report is of the lookup results, not of the named area, so the builder's output would have to carry a second measure.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Reorders the run's stages to remove one call; the cost and the risk are out of proportion to the defect.
